title: Staged activation fragmentation and hierarchical scratch manager
author: Priya Nair
commits: initial staged activation fragmentation scheduler prototype
add hierarchical scratch manager and allocator hooks
integrate staged ckpt with continuous batching path
tests: add microbenchmarks for workspace usage and KV interaction
docs: runtime tuning guide for staged ckpt and scratch tiers
fix: tighten fallback logic for tiny tensors to avoid regression
description:
Summary: Introduces a staged activation fragmentation scheduler paired with a hierarchical scratch manager to reduce peak GPU workspace and overall activation memory for long-sequence and mixed-size workloads. The staged scheduler splits activation checkpointing into smaller, cache-friendly fragments (stages) and schedules them with awareness of the continuous batching router and KV cache hotset. The hierarchical scratch manager introduces two scratch tiers: 'fast' per-stream scratch (small, low-latency allocations) and 'pool' shared scratch (larger, coalesced allocations) that are reclaimed opportunistically.

Motivation: On real workloads we observe that monolithic checkpoint regions and one-size scratch arenas cause both elevated peak workspace usage and fragmentation that prevents re-use across requests. This is especially acute for mixed token-length traffic where continuous batching mixes short and very long sequences into the same batch and wastes both GPU local memory and workspace reserved by kernels. The goal is a pragmatic runtime change that gives ~20% peak GPU memory reduction on mixed workloads with no regression in p99 latency and minimal behavioral change for existing deployments.

Design: 1) Staged Activation Fragmentation: Instead of checkpointing an entire layer group, the scheduler fragments checkpoints into small stages (configurable by fragment_size_tokens). The runtime tracks stage dependencies and issues evictions of intermediate activations earlier while ensuring correctness. Fragment sizes are chosen to align with attention-kernel-friendly boundaries to keep kernel selection optimal. 2) Hierarchical Scratch Manager: Scratch allocations are categorized by size and lifetime. Fast-tier allocations are bounded and tied to a stream; pool-tier allocations are large contiguous blocks drawn from a slab allocator that prefers coalesced re-use. The manager communicates with the kernel selector to request 'scratch hints' so kernels can express preferred tier and alignment. 3) Continuous batching integration: The continuous_batch_router is extended to prefer grouping fragments from the same request into near-term execution windows, reducing KV cache thrash and allowing scratch re-use across micro-batches. 4) KV cache awareness: The staged scheduler exposes a hotset hint API so the KV eviction policy can avoid thrashing frequently-reused prefixes during staged recomputation.

Compatibility & Config: All features are behind runtime flags: STAGED_CKPT_ENABLED (default: off for stable rollout), STAGED_FRAGMENT_SIZE (tokens, default: 512), HIER_SCRATCH_ENABLED (default: on), SCRATCH_FAST_LIMIT (bytes). Defaults chosen to be conservative; non-enabled code path is exactly previous behavior.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks (benchmarks/lab/staged_ckpt_memory_profile.csv) and end-to-end evals on benchmark-lab show: - Mixed traffic (short=16, mid=256, long=2048, 8x concurrency): peak GPU resident memory reduced by 18-24% depending on model shape. - Workspace (scratch) allocations reduced by 28-33% for assemblies using fused attention kernels. - P50 latency unchanged within +/-1%, p99 unchanged within +/-2% after tuning fragment_size_tokens. - Small regression in single-request startup time (+2-3%) due to additional scheduling overhead, amortized in steady-state.

Sample API hint (C++) used between kernel and scratch manager:

// kernel requests scratch hint
ScratchHint hint;
hint.preferred_tier = ScratchTier::FAST;
hint.min_bytes = 1 << 16; // 64KB
manager->RequestScratch(hint, &scratch_handle);

Test plan: - Unit tests for staged_ckpt_scheduler state-machine and correctness (runtime/batching/tests/bench_staged_ckpt.cpp). - Integration tests validating KV hotset invariants with staged recomputation (runtime/kv/kv_cache_integration_test.cpp). - CI presubmit runs include memory-pressure scenarios and a small matrix of fragment_size values. - Canary rollout: opt-in via feature flags for dedicated clusters, 2% of traffic for 48h, then gradual ramp.

Rollout & Observability: Added metrics: staged_ckpt.fragments_started, staged_ckpt.fragments_completed, scratch.reuse_rate_fast, scratch.pool_fragmentation_pct. Alerts added for unexpected growth in fragments in-flight and low scratch reuse. Docs updated with tuning guidance and a suggested checklist.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc + diagrams in PR thread - [x] Microbenchmarks attached - [x] Integration tests for KV interactions - [x] API compatibility non-breaking - [x] Observability and alerts - [x] Docs and examples

Notes: This PR attempts to balance additional scheduler complexity against the memory wins. For very small models or very uniform token-length traffic the feature toggles provide minimal benefit; those workloads can keep defaults. The staged fragmentation thresholds were tuned using the benchmark-lab trace corpus.
